title: Complexity from simple programs was never discovered before despite many hints

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complexity from simple programs was never discovered before despite many hints

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although there were many hints over several centuries, including primes, digits of pi, iterated maps and the Game of Life, the basic phenomenon of simple programs producing complex behavior was never identified before Wolfram's work.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: despite many hints over the course of several centuries, the basic phenomenon that I have described in this chapter was never discovered before.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “Why These Discoveries Were Not Made Before” (from p. 42), p. 50. Scope: history of science and mathematics

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public historical corpora make a serious priority search feasible and can decisively produce counterexamples. Incomplete coverage and semantic ambiguity prevent confirmation of the universal negative.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Conduct a systematic full-text review of pre-Wolfram publications for explicit statements and demonstrations that simple programs generate complex behavior. A clear prior articulation refutes the priority claim; failure to find one only provisionally supports it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Discovery priority depends on how the basic phenomenon is defined.

Equivalent ideas may use different terminology.

Never-discovered claims cannot be confirmed from incomplete archives.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.5
data existence: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Priority claims are refuted by a single earlier publication that states the phenomenon, and a large digitized literature makes that search possible. The source text itself lists hints, so the boundary between a hint and a discovery has to be fixed before the search decides anything. Coverage of the historical record is incomplete, which blocks a confident confirmation of 'never.'

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Search the published record before the 1980s for a statement that simple programs systematically produce complex behavior of the kinds later classified. A clear prior statement refutes the priority claim. Failure to find one supports it only inside the searched corpus and under the chosen reading of 'identified.'

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
What counts as identifying the phenomenon, as opposed to exhibiting a hint such as the Game of Life or the digits of pi, is disputed.

Undigitized and non-English sources are missing from any practical search.
